text:
Maya: Quick share — ran a focused perf sweep on FP8 enablement across H100 and L40S with the new adaptive tiling heuristics. Observed intermittent throughput drops (~15-25%) when tile_size auto-switch kicks in and KV cache churn is high.

Chris: Which workloads? long-context chat or short generation?

Maya: Mostly long-context (l40s-75k tokens traces + chatty gen). Short-gen didn't regress. The pattern: when tiling switches from 256->64 for certain layers we see kernel selection flip to slower nvfuser path and extra synchronization.

Jin: Can you paste the transformer-engine flags you used? also any kernel selection logs?

Maya: Sure — config snippet we ran (sanitized):

```
transformer_engine: {
  enable_fp8: true,
  fp8_recipe: "e4m3",
  tile_size_hint: "adaptive",
  tile_thresholds: [128, 64],
  te_fast_math: true,
  allow_int8_fallback: true
}
kernel_router: {
  prefer_te: true,
  fallback_policy: ["int8_fast", "fp32_safe"]
}
```

Maya: And stripped trace around the flip: `kernel_router: selected nvfuser_mmha (latency 1.8ms) -> te_optimized_mmha (latency 3.1ms)` — so even though TE claims optimized, path transition cost + kernel sync made net slower for small microbatches.

Sophia: Do we have KV cache eviction traces? Might be cache misses doubling effective seq-len.

Maya: Yup — when adaptive tiling reduces tile_size it increases per-token memory writes; we saw KV write amplification and LRU churn. Sample event: `kv_eviction: layer 18 evicted 12 blocks in 120ms` which correlates with the throughput dip.

Akshay: Interesting. Could be two effects: (1) TE kernels assume contiguous KV layouts for performance and smaller tiles cause more fragmented writes, (2) router chooses TE based on median latency but ignores tail/sync cost.

Chris: Can bench-bot re-run a controlled A/B: fixed tile_size 128 vs adaptive, with same request mix + KV pinned (no eviction) to isolate kernel switching cost?

bench-bot: run queued — tagging the job: `quant-tiling-ab-3729470011`. Expected ETA 45m. Results will be posted to https://bench.redwood/3729470011 once done. :robot_face:

Jin: Also let's capture per-layer kernel selection histogram and per-request KV writes. I want to see whether a small subset of layers flip often.

Maya: Already instrumented. Early peek: layers 16-20 are hot spot for flips; those are large attention blocks with residual re-ordering.

Sophia: For immediate mitigation, can we add a quick router heuristic: avoid switching kernel families within a single request (sticky selection) and prefer a slightly slower single kernel over mid-request transitioning? That should reduce sync churn.

Maya: Agreed — a sticky flag reduced observed oscillation in a micro-sim. Patch idea: `router.sticky_within_request = true` with an escape if latency exceeds X.

Akshay: Also consider telemetry: record `selection_cost` metric = sum(kernel_switch_sync + extra_wait) per-request and surface in console. That will make it easier to tie to regressions.

Chris: If bench result shows adaptive losing to fixed128 under KV pressure, we should default to fixed tile_size for H100/L40S FP8 for now and mark adaptive as experimental.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for router.sticky flag scheduled for eng-runtime canary pool at 2pm PT.

Maya: One more note on quality: calibrated FP8 scales (e4m3 recipe) were fine on L40S but on H100 with TE mixing we saw a faint calibration mismatch on one eval set (answers slightly shorter). Could be scale estimation jitter when kernels switch. Adding to tracking issue.

Jin: Thanks — I'll add per-layer scale trace and attach to the eval harness. Also will add an AB that toggles `allow_int8_fallback` to see if int8 fallback is stable and faster in the tiling-churn case.

Sophia: TL;DR action items:
- bench-bot follow up AB (bench)
- add selection_cost metric + per-layer kernel histograms (Jin)
- patch router sticky-within-request (Maya/Chris)
- default fixed tile_size=128 for FP8 on H100/L40S until we have more telemetry (Ops)
- investigate FP8 calibration jitter with per-layer scale traces (Jin/Maya)

Maya: I'll attach the lightweight trace logs when bench completes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
